name: Session recording
summary: The session itself is recorded, not merely the page view.

mechanism.what: A session-recording script captures behaviour inside the page: mouse movement, scrolling, clicks and often keystrokes in form fields, replayable afterwards as a film of the visit.
mechanism.why_it_matters: This is a different order of collection from counting page views. What someone typed and then deleted, where they hesitated, which field they returned to: none of that is needed to run a website, and all of it is revealing.
common_causes: recording script loaded outside the consent gate
field masking left off, so entered text is captured too
mechanism.not_this: Ordinary page-view analytics is not this entry. The distinguishing feature is capture of in-page behaviour.

detection.indicator: A request to a session-recording endpoint of a recording vendor, carrying a site identifier, at page load.
capture_requirements: note whether field masking is active; unmasked input raises the stakes considerably

falsifiers.condition: The vendor processes only aggregated data without session capture.
Recording starts only after consent is granted.
All input fields are masked at source.

methods.expect: a request to a recording vendor endpoint before consent

rebuttals.objection: The recording servers are in the EU.
rebuttals.answer: Where the recording is stored says nothing about whether it should have been made. Location is a separate question from lawfulness of collection.

does_not_establish: harm; the catalogue standardises a finding so it can be referred to, it does not weigh it
severity; there is no score here, by design. Weighing belongs to whoever applies the entry to a concrete case
unlawfulness; that is for a supervisory authority or a court
intent; a fault is usually a build decision, not a plan
absence: not finding it in one capture is not evidence that it is not there

in_practice.dpia: Verify whether in-page behaviour is captured and whether input fields are masked, rather than treating it as analytics.
in_practice.procurement: No session recording is active before consent, and where used, input masking is enabled and demonstrated.
in_practice.complaint: A capture showing the recording endpoint contacted at load, and whether field masking was active.
in_practice.audit_question: Is anything recording mouse movement or keystrokes, and from what moment?
